column2: [troublemaker_child.GetFirstName] snatched my wooden sword in the yard and will not give it back. [troublemaker_child.GetSheHeCap] is laughing and waving it over [troublemaker_child.GetHerHis] head, daring me to come and take it.
Knock [troublemaker_child.GetHerHim] down and take it back!
Fine, we can take turns.
They will hear of it.
They will hear of it.

[shy_child.GetFirstName] never plays with the rest of us. [shy_child.GetSheHeCap] sits under the stairs with a book, and the bigger children pull [shy_child.GetHerHis] hair and throw [shy_child.GetHerHis] books in the moat.
I will teach [shy_child.GetHerHim] to stand up for [shy_child.GetHerHim]self.
[shy_child.GetFirstName] decides what to do.
[shy_child.GetSheHeCap] can borrow my wooden sword.
[shy_child.GetFirstName] decides what to do.
Books are for the dull. Leave [shy_child.GetHerHim] to them.
[From.GetFirstName] says the next time the big children come for my books I must hit the biggest one on the nose, as hard as I can, and the rest will run away.
Next time, I fight back!
[From.GetFirstName] will see the result.
I cannot. I just cannot.

[From.GetFirstName] has offered me [From.GetHerHis] wooden sword, so that the others will leave me alone. It is chipped, and the hilt is wrapped in string, and it is the best thing anyone has ever given me.
Thank you!
I do not want it. Swords are for brutes.
I told [From.GetFirstName] to stand up for [From.GetHerHim]self, and [From.GetSheHe] did. The first nose [From.GetSheHe] hit, as hard as [From.GetSheHe] could, was mine.
The cheek!
Well struck! I taught you that.

My guardian caught me asleep in the hayloft when I should have been at my letters, and was reaching for the switch when [helping_child.GetFirstName] spoke up and swore it was [helping_child.GetHerHis] fault for keeping me up all night.
Thank [helping_child.GetHerHim] with all my heart.
[helping_child.GetFirstName] is thanked.
Nobody asked [helping_child.GetHerHim] to interfere.
[helping_child.GetFirstName] is not thanked.
Own up. It was my laziness, not [helping_child.GetHerHis].
I took a thrashing that was meant for [From.GetFirstName], and [From.GetSheHe] has not stopped thanking me since.
I took a thrashing that was meant for [From.GetFirstName], and [From.GetSheHe] told everyone I should mind my own business.
A friend for life.
Ingrate! I will never help [From.GetHerHim] again.
Let it go.
I will remember this.

[shy_courtier.GetFirstName] goes red as a beet whenever a lady so much as says good morning to him. Last night at supper one asked him to pass the salt and he knocked over a jug of wine and fled the hall.
Offer to teach him a few things.
[shy_courtier.GetFirstName] hears your offer.
Not my problem.
[From.GetFirstName], who can talk to any lady at court and make her laugh, has offered to teach me how it is done.
Gratefully!
I can manage alone, thank you!
Thank you, but no.
I offered to help [From.GetFirstName] with the ladies, and he told me to keep my nose out of his affairs.
I offered to help [From.GetFirstName] with the ladies, and he thanked me very politely and said no.
Ungrateful pup.
As he wishes.
Every lady at court looks straight through me. [lustful_courtier.GetFirstName], on the other hand, has them laughing at every word. Perhaps he could tell me how.
Ask him for help.
[lustful_courtier.GetFirstName] is asked.
Pay him for lessons.
[lustful_courtier.GetFirstName] is offered your money.
I will die alone.
[From.GetFirstName] has asked me, red to the ears, to teach him how to talk to women.
Such secrets do not come cheap.
[From.GetFirstName] hears your price.
For a friend, nothing.
Laugh in his face.
[From.GetFirstName] will teach me everything he knows about women, for ten gold pieces.
Here is the money.
I keep my pride and my purse.
[From.GetFirstName] has pressed a purse into my hand and begged me to teach him how to talk to women.
Throw the purse back at him.
Take the money and teach him.
[From.GetFirstName] gets his lessons.
Give it back and teach him as a friend.

The lessons from [From.GetFirstName] are humiliating. I have had to bow to a broom, compliment a hound and recite poetry to the cook. But last night, a lady laughed at something I said, and not unkindly.
There may be hope for me yet.
[child_2.GetFirstName] is reading the same book as me, the one about the dragon and the seven knights, and has already worked out who poisoned the old king.
We should be friends!
[child_2.GetFirstName] hears your offer.
There can only be one cleverest girl at court.
Keep my books to myself.
[From.GetFirstName] wants to be my friend. We like the same books and the same games, and she is nearly as clever as me.
Yes!
Never. She copies everything I do.
[target_courtier.GetFirstName] flutters her eyelashes at every page and squire at court, and they follow her about like puppies. When I try, they ask if I have something in my eye.
Ask her secret.
[target_courtier.GetFirstName] is asked.
I cannot stand her.
Watch, and envy.
[From.GetFirstName], who never says a word to a boy, has asked me to teach her how to make them follow her about.
Of course! Watch closely.
Find your own boys.
Laugh at her.

[target_courtier.GetFirstName] flirts with every man at court, married or not, and somehow everyone adores her for it. If I so much as smile at a knight, the gossip goes round the court twice before supper.
Ask how she does it.
[target_courtier.GetFirstName] is asked.
Shameless creature.
Each to her own.
[From.GetFirstName], who blushes if a man so much as looks at her, has asked me how I make them all fall over themselves.
Teach her everything.
[From.GetFirstName] hears your answer.
Find your own admirers.
[From.GetFirstName] hears your answer.
A few hints, no more.
[From.GetFirstName] has taken me under her wing. I have learned more about men in a week than in all my life.
[From.GetFirstName] gave me a few hints, kindly enough, and then went back to her admirers.
A friend!
That was kind of her.
[From.GetFirstName] laughed when I asked her for help, and told everyone at court.
I will never forgive her.
[target_courtier.GetFirstName] put me on my back in the sword yard in three strokes, in front of everyone, and is still grinning about it.
Shake [target_courtier.GetHerHis] hand. [target_courtier.GetSheHeCap] won fairly.
I will have my revenge!
Practise until I am better.
[target_courtier.GetFirstName] trips me in the corridors, puts frogs in my bed and calls me names in front of the others. I do not even know what I did.
Hit [target_courtier.GetHerHim] back.
Offer [target_courtier.GetHerHim] a honey cake.
[target_courtier.GetFirstName] is offered a honey cake.
[target_courtier.GetSheHeCap] will tire of it.
[From.GetFirstName], whom I have been tormenting for weeks, has offered me a honey cake.
Eat it, and put a frog in [From.GetHerHis] bed anyway.
[From.GetFirstName] finds the frog.
Eat it, and leave [From.GetHerHim] alone.
[From.GetFirstName] is left alone.
[From.GetFirstName] ate my honey cake and put a frog in my bed anyway.
At least I tried to be kind.
Try once more. Everyone needs a friend.
[From.GetFirstName] ate my honey cake and has not bothered me since. Yesterday [From.GetSheHe] even said good morning.
Ask [From.GetHerHim] to play.
Leave it at peace.

I cannot stand [target_courtier.GetFirstName]. The way [target_courtier.GetSheHe] laughs, the way [target_courtier.GetSheHe] eats, the way everyone likes [target_courtier.GetHerHim]. I do not know why. I just cannot.
Make [target_courtier.GetHerHis] life a misery.
Pray for a better heart.
Tell [target_courtier.GetHerHim] so, to [target_courtier.GetHerHis] face.
[target_courtier.GetFirstName] is told.
[From.GetFirstName] walked up to me in the yard and told me, in front of everyone, that [From.GetSheHe] cannot stand me.
The feeling is mutual!
Why? What did I do?
[From.GetFirstName] is asked why.
I do not care what [From.GetSheHe] thinks.
[From.GetFirstName] wants to know what [From.GetSheHe] ever did to me. I cannot think of a single thing.
Nothing. Let us start again.
[From.GetFirstName] hears your answer.
You exist.
[From.GetFirstName] hears your answer.
[From.GetFirstName] says I never did anything to [From.GetHerHim], and wants to start again.
I asked [From.GetFirstName] what I ever did to [From.GetHerHim]. "You exist," [From.GetSheHe] said.
Friends, then.
Then we are enemies.
I heard one of the other children at court say the gods are a story for babies, and that the priests only want our money. I nearly fainted.
Pray for the poor fool.
Show the poor fool the light.
The doubter hears your sermon.
[From.GetFirstName] has followed me about all day, telling me about the gods, the saints and what happens to children who laugh at them.
Go away!
Pretend to see the light, so [From.GetSheHe] will stop.
[From.GetFirstName] believes you.
Perhaps [From.GetSheHe] is right...
[From.GetFirstName] has saved a soul.
I have brought [From.GetFirstName] to the gods! [From.GetSheHeCap] says [From.GetSheHe] will pray every night from now on.
The gods be praised.
[From.GetFirstName] came to the shrine with me today, and prayed, and meant it. I have saved a soul.
The gods be praised!
The ladies of the court gathered round [embroidery_prodigy.GetFirstName]'s needlework today, a stag hunt in seven colours. Nobody looked at mine.
She is better than me.
I hate her.
Unpick her stitches in the night.
[embroidery_prodigy.GetFirstName] finds her work ruined.
Ask her to teach me.
[embroidery_prodigy.GetFirstName] is asked.
Someone crept into the solar in the night and unpicked my stag hunt, three months of work, stitch by stitch. [From.GetFirstName] cannot stop smiling.
I know who did this.
Begin again.
[From.GetFirstName] has asked me to teach her my stitches.
Gladly!
My secrets are my own.
My doll is gone! [doll_stealer.GetFirstName] has it, I know it, I saw it under her arm this morning.
Get it back!
[doll_stealer.GetFirstName] decides.
Cry.
[From.GetFirstName] has found out that I took her doll and wants it back.
Give it back, and say sorry.
[From.GetFirstName] gets her doll back.
Give it back. It is ugly anyway.
Finders keepers!
[From.GetFirstName] does not get her doll back.
[From.GetFirstName] gave my doll back and said she was sorry, and we played with it together all afternoon.
[From.GetFirstName] gave my doll back and said it was ugly anyway.
[From.GetFirstName] will not give my doll back. She says finders keepers.
A new friend!
At least I have my doll.
I will get her for this!
[fellow_crusader.GetTitledFirstName] rides beside me on this holy war, sworn to the same faith and the same vow. Tomorrow we meet the enemy.
Pray beside [fellow_crusader.GetHerHim] before the battle.
[fellow_crusader.GetTitledFirstName] sees what you do.
Race [fellow_crusader.GetHerHim] to the enemy banner!
Count the plunder.
This crusade is not mine. I am going home.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] knelt beside me all night before the battle and prayed until dawn. Some say [From.GetSheHe] prayed more loudly than [From.GetSheHe] needed to.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] rode ahead of me into the enemy and took the banner I was riding for. The whole army is singing [From.GetHerHis] name.
A brother in faith.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] will hear of it.
A rival for the same glory.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] will hear of it.
This crusade is not mine. I am going home.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] tells anyone who will listen that my prayers before the battle were for show.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] tells anyone who will listen that I stole the banner from under [From.GetHerHis] nose.
Then we are rivals.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] came to me after the battle and said that my prayers had steadied [From.GetHerHis] hand.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] came to me after the battle and raised a cup to the one who took the banner.
A friend for the road.
I want a seat on my liege's council, and [bond_mentor.GetTitledFirstName] already has one. No one knows the work better.
Ask [bond_mentor.GetHerHim] to teach me.
[bond_mentor.GetTitledFirstName] is asked.
Study alone.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] wants to learn my craft. Whether it is to serve the realm or to take my seat, [From.GetSheHe] did not say.
Teach [From.GetHerHim] everything.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] learns.
Teach [From.GetHerHim], and watch [From.GetHerHim].
[From.GetSheHeCap] wants my seat. Get out.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has taught me more of the council's work in a season than I learned in years, and we have become friends over the ledgers.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] taught me well enough, but never once turned [From.GetHerHis] back on me.
I have learned much.
[bond_mother.GetTitledFirstName] is with child too, and as uncomfortable as I am. We have taken to sitting together in the garden with our feet up, complaining.
Share our aches and hopes.
[bond_mother.GetTitledFirstName] becomes your friend.
Rest, and keep my own counsel.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] and I sit in the garden every afternoon, comparing ankles and arguing over names.
A true friend.
Only until the babies come.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] will find out after the birth.
Since the babies came, [From.GetTitledFirstName] has not had a moment for me. I suppose the garden and the complaining were all [From.GetSheHe] wanted.
So much for friendship.
[From.GetFirstName] and I are friends now! We are going to build a fort in the woods and nobody else is allowed in.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] and I are friends now.
A friend!
[From.GetFirstName] is my enemy now, forever and ever.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has made it plain that we are rivals.
So be it.

A rider in [friend_at_war.GetTitledFirstName]'s colours came to my gate at dusk, his horse lathered to the knees. My friend is at war, and the letter he carries does not ask for anything, not in so many words. It only says the enemy is many, the roads are long, and that [friend_at_war.GetSheHe] thinks of me often.
Sound the horns. We ride to [friend_at_war.GetHerHis] side.
I cannot send swords, but I can send gold.
It is not my war.
[friend_at_war.GetTitledFirstName] will hear that you are coming.
[friend_at_war.GetTitledFirstName] will receive the gold.
[friend_at_war.GetTitledFirstName] may learn that you did nothing.

My dear friend,

Your letter reached me in the camp, and I read it out to my captains so they would know that we do not stand alone. My banners are already on the road. Hold fast until we come.

[From.GetTitledFirstName]
A true friend!

My dear friend,

I am no soldier and my levies are not what yours are, but gold buys swords as well as any oath. Take this, pay your men, and win.

[From.GetTitledFirstName]
That will keep the sellswords honest.

The war is over, or as good as, and in all these months not one word came from [From.GetTitledFirstName]. No banners, no gold, not even a letter wishing me luck. My heralds say [From.GetSheHe] spent the summer hunting.
Some friend.
We won without [From.GetHerHim]. Let the bards say so.

The war goes hard. My captains count the dead each morning and the treasury each evening, and neither count pleases me. [friend_ally.GetTitledFirstName] has been my friend for years and sits at peace behind [friend_ally.GetHerHis] walls. One letter could change that.
Ask [friend_ally.GetHerHim] to fight beside me.
Ask [friend_ally.GetHerHim] for gold.
I will fight my own wars.
[friend_ally.GetTitledFirstName] will read your letter.

My dear friend,

You will have heard that I am at war. I would not ask if I were not hard pressed, but I am, and I have no one else to ask. Bring your banners. Stand beside me as I would stand beside you.

[From.GetTitledFirstName]

My dear friend,

You will have heard that I am at war. I do not ask you to spill blood for me, only to help me pay those who will. My coffers are bare and the sellswords do not fight on promises.

[From.GetTitledFirstName]
Muster my army. My friend's war is mine.
Send gold. It is the least I can do.
I am sorry, but I cannot help.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] will hear that you have joined.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] will receive the gold.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] will hear that you will not help.
Banners on the hills! [From.GetTitledFirstName] has kept faith, and [From.GetHerHis] army marches to join mine. My men cheered when they saw the colours.
I will not forget this.
A chest of gold has come from [From.GetTitledFirstName], with a letter wishing me victory. It will keep the sellswords in the field for another season.
Gold is good. Swords would have been better.

My dear friend,

I wish with all my heart that I could help, but I cannot. Forgive me.

[From.GetTitledFirstName]
Forgive? Never.

[friend_link.GetTitledFirstName] keeps talking about [friend_new.GetTitledFirstName]. "You two would get on famously," [friend_link.GetSheHe] says, every time we meet. Now [friend_link.GetSheHe] wants to bring us together at last.
I would be glad to meet [friend_new.GetHerHim].
I have friends enough.
[friend_new.GetTitledFirstName] decides what to make of you.
[friend_new.GetTitledFirstName] will feel snubbed.
[friend_link.GetTitledFirstName] will be annoyed.

[friend_link.GetTitledFirstName] has finally brought me together with [From.GetTitledFirstName], of whom I have heard so much. We have shared a jug of wine and a long evening, and I have made up my mind about [From.GetHerHim].
A friend of my friend is a friend of mine.
I cannot stand [From.GetHerHim].
A polite word, no more.
[friend_link.GetTitledFirstName] will be pleased.
[friend_link.GetTitledFirstName] will be displeased.
I had looked forward to meeting [From.GetTitledFirstName]. It seems [From.GetSheHe] did not feel the same. I have been snubbed, and in front of a friend.
I will remember this.
My two friends [friend_asker.GetFirstName] and [friend_new.GetFirstName] sat up half the night laughing at each other's stories. I knew they would.
I am a fine judge of people.
I told [From.GetTitledFirstName] what a fine friend [friend_new.GetFirstName] would make. [From.GetSheHeCap] said [From.GetSheHe] had friends enough. What am I, then, one of the crowd?

I brought [From.GetTitledFirstName] together with my friend [friend_asker.GetFirstName], and [From.GetSheHe] gave [friend_asker.GetHerHim] a polite word and the back of [From.GetHerHis] head. I was ashamed.
How rude.
I brought [From.GetTitledFirstName] together with my friend [friend_asker.GetFirstName], and now they hate each other. They glare across every room they share, and each expects me to take a side.
This is [From.GetFirstName]'s doing.

[heretic_friend.GetTitledFirstName] has fallen in with heretics. [heretic_friend.GetSheHeCap] speaks of the true faith with a sneer now and quotes teachings I was raised to call lies. The priests have noticed, and so have my enemies, who say a friend of a heretic is half a heretic.

[heretic_friend.GetTitledFirstName] has turned to another cult. [heretic_friend.GetSheHeCap] makes offerings at other altars now and calls other gods first in [heretic_friend.GetHerHis] prayers. The faithful of our gods have quarrelled over such things for centuries, and the priests have noticed.
I will bring [heretic_friend.GetHerHim] back to the true faith.
[heretic_friend.GetHerHisCap] faith is [heretic_friend.GetHerHis] own affair.
Tell me of it. What do you see there?
I will not call a heretic my friend!
One god or another, what does it matter?
[heretic_friend.GetTitledFirstName] will hear you out.
[heretic_friend.GetTitledFirstName] will be glad of it.
[heretic_friend.GetTitledFirstName] will tell you of [heretic_friend.GetHerHis] faith.
The friendship is over.

[From.GetTitledFirstName] has come to me with a book of scripture under [From.GetHerHis] arm and tears in [From.GetHerHis] eyes. [From.GetSheHeCap] begs me to give up my faith and come back to [From.GetHerHis], for the sake of my soul and our friendship.
How dare [From.GetSheHe]! Get out!
Perhaps [From.GetSheHe] is right.
Let us not quarrel over gods.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] will rejoice.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] will be disappointed.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has told me that my faith is my own affair, and that a friend is a friend whatever altar [From.GetSheHe] kneels at. The priests will not like it.
A true friend.

[heretic_friend.GetTitledFirstName] talked of [heretic_friend.GetHerHis] faith long into the night, of its gods and its promises and the peace [heretic_friend.GetSheHe] has found there. Much of it was strange to me. Some of it was not.
[heretic_friend.GetSheHeCap] has opened my eyes.
Fine words, but I keep my own gods.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has made it known that [From.GetSheHe] will not call me friend while I hold to my faith.
Then we are done.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has come back to the true faith! The priests are delighted, and so am I.
Praise the gods!
[From.GetTitledFirstName] listened to everything I had to say, smiled, and said we should not quarrel over gods. [From.GetSheHeCap] has not changed [From.GetHerHis] mind one bit.
[From.GetSheHeCap] will burn for it, and I cannot stop it.

At council and at feasts I stumble over my words, while [friend_tutor.GetTitledFirstName] could talk a dwarf out of his gold. [friend_tutor.GetSheHeCap] is my friend. Surely [friend_tutor.GetSheHe] would teach me a little of the art.
Ask for lessons.
Practise alone, before a mirror.
Your friend decides whether to help.

In the practice yard I am clumsy and on the field I am slow, and everyone can see it. My friend [friend_tutor.GetTitledFirstName] is a far better warrior than I will ever be, unless [friend_tutor.GetSheHe] teaches me.
Ask for lessons.
Train alone until my arms ache.

The ledgers do not add up, the granaries are half empty, and I cannot say where the money went. My friend [friend_tutor.GetTitledFirstName] keeps accounts that balance to the last penny. [friend_tutor.GetSheHeCap] might tell me how.
Ask for advice.
The ledgers will teach me, if I sit with them long enough.

There are whispers at court that I never hear until it is too late. My friend [friend_tutor.GetTitledFirstName] hears all of them, and some say [friend_tutor.GetSheHe] starts half of them. I could learn a great deal from [friend_tutor.GetHerHim].
Ask to be taught.
I will learn by watching.
I stumble through the holy texts and lose my place in the prayers. My friend [friend_tutor.GetTitledFirstName] is learned and devout, and could teach me to read scripture as the priests do.
Ask to be taught.
I will pray alone.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has asked me, rather shyly, to teach [From.GetHerHim] how to speak at council and charm at feasts. [From.GetSheHeCap] says I could talk a dwarf out of his gold.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has asked me to teach [From.GetHerHim] to fight. [From.GetSheHeCap] is clumsy in the practice yard and knows it.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has asked me to look over [From.GetHerHis] ledgers and teach [From.GetHerHim] to keep accounts. From the look of them, it will take a while.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has asked me, in a low voice and a quiet corner, to teach [From.GetHerHim] how to hear the whispers at court.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has asked me to teach [From.GetHerHim] to read the holy texts properly. [From.GetSheHeCap] loses [From.GetHerHis] place in the prayers.
Gladly.
I have no time for it.
Friendship is one thing, my time another. I will want paying.
You will teach your friend.
Your friend will be disappointed.
Your friend decides whether to pay.

For weeks [friend_tutor.GetTitledFirstName] has made me speak before a mirror, stopped me every time I mumbled, and laughed at my jokes only when they were funny. Yesterday at council I spoke, and they listened.
For weeks [friend_tutor.GetTitledFirstName] has put me on my back in the practice yard every morning. This morning, for the first time, I put [friend_tutor.GetHerHim] on [friend_tutor.GetHerHis].
For weeks [friend_tutor.GetTitledFirstName] has gone through my ledgers line by line. We found two dishonest reeves, a granary that does not exist and a much better way of keeping accounts.
For weeks [friend_tutor.GetTitledFirstName] has shown me who listens at which door, who pays whom, and which servants can be bought. I will never look at my court the same way again.
For weeks [friend_tutor.GetTitledFirstName] has read the holy texts with me by candlelight. I understand them now as I never did before, and the priests have noticed.
Thank you, my friend.
[friend_tutor.GetTitledFirstName] says [friend_tutor.GetSheHe] has no time to teach me. [friend_tutor.GetSheHeCap] had time enough to go hunting yesterday.
I thought we were friends.
[friend_tutor.GetTitledFirstName] will teach me, [friend_tutor.GetSheHe] says, but [friend_tutor.GetHerHis] time is worth gold, friend or no friend.
Pay [friend_tutor.GetHerHim]. Knowledge is worth it.
A friend should not ask.
[friend_tutor.GetTitledFirstName] will hear that you will not pay.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] would not pay for my lessons. [From.GetSheHeCap] says a friend should not ask. A friend should not expect my time for nothing, either.
Then [From.GetSheHe] can stay ignorant.

[way_friend.GetTitledFirstName] has forsworn the flesh. No lovers, no feasts, no wine, only prayer and the cold calm of someone who wants nothing. Now that I have heirs, I sometimes wonder what that calm feels like.
Ask [way_friend.GetHerHim] how [way_friend.GetSheHe] bears it.
Tease [way_friend.GetHerHim] about it.
Each to their own.
Your friend decides what to tell you.
Your friend will be annoyed.
[way_friend.GetTitledFirstName] lives for wine, song and the bedchamber, and never seems to tire of any of them. [way_friend.GetSheHeCap] laughs more than anyone I know.
Ask [way_friend.GetHerHim] to show me how.
Tell [way_friend.GetHerHim] what I think of it.
Each to their own.

[way_friend.GetTitledFirstName] lives among books. [way_friend.GetSheHeCap] reads at table, reads in the bath, and once walked into a well while reading. [way_friend.GetSheHeCap] seems happier than anyone has a right to be.
Ask what [way_friend.GetSheHe] finds in them.
Tease the bookworm.
Each to their own.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has asked how I live without lovers or wine. [From.GetSheHeCap] seems to want to know, not to mock.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has asked me to show [From.GetHerHim] how to live as I do. [From.GetSheHeCap] has spent too long being sensible.
